mentions.name: Larm
mentions.description: This app is an uptime monitoring service designed to be genuinely reliable and to only alert users when something is actually going wrong. It includes polished status pages, offers a free tier sufficient for most users (with a paid tier gating expensive features like SMS alerts), and provides a public response time checker tool powered by its probe infrastructure.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’ve been building an uptime monitor service for a while now, something that is genuinely reliable and only alerts you when something is actually going on. Also comes with very pretty status pages!

mentions.name: Larm
mentions.description: An uptime monitoring service focused on reliability and reduction in false positives. It features a Phoenix LiveView dashboard, Go probes running on four continents connected to the backend via websocket tunnels, and ClickHouse for reporting, plus a CLI and an MCP interface. A free response time checking tool lets users test how fast their site is.
mentions.problem: False positives and unreliable results in uptime monitoring.
mentions.audience: Built for the author's own use, shared in case others find it useful.
mentions.source_excerpt: https://larm.dev, an uptime monitoring service with a focus on reliability and reduction in false positives. I’ve been building it for myself really but I figure it’s worth sharing it with people in case someone else finds it useful too.
